passage:
A van is traveling at a constant speed of $54	ext{ km}\cdot	ext{h}^{-1}$ in a $40	ext{ km}\cdot	ext{h}^{-1}$ zone.

A policeman starts his car from rest just as the van passes him.

The police car accelerates at $2	ext{ m}\cdot	ext{s}^{-2}$ until it reaches a maximum velocity of $20	ext{ m}\cdot	ext{s}^{-1}$.
The policeman then continues driving at this constant velocity.
question: Calculate how far the police car has to travel before it catches up with the van.
memo:
$x_{	ext{police car}} = x_{	ext{van}} \checkmark$
For police car: $x_p = 100 + 20 \Delta t$
For van: $x_v = 150 + 15 \Delta t$
$100 + 20\Delta t = 150 + 15\Delta t \checkmark$
$5\Delta t = 50 \implies \Delta t = 10	ext{ s}$ (after reaching max velocity)
Total distance $x = 100 + 20(10) = 300	ext{ m} \checkmark$
The police car catches up with the van after $300	ext{ m}$ $\checkmark$ after $20	ext{ s}$ $\checkmark$

passage: A steel ball of mass $5\text{ kg}$ is rolling over a frictionless surface. When the ball reaches point A it has mechanical energy of $250\text{ J}$.
question: Determine whether the mechanical energy acquired by the ball at point A will be enough to carry the ball over point D. Show ALL calculations.
memo:
Mechanical energy at point D $= E_{\text{K}} + E_{\text{P}} = 0 + (5)(9.8)(7)\checkmark = 343\text{ J}$
The minimum energy needed for the steel ball to reach point D is $343\text{ J}\checkmark$
The mechanical energy of the steel ball is $250\text{ J}$ which is less than that at D $\checkmark$
So the ball cannot reach point D. $\checkmark$
final_answer: No, the ball cannot reach point D as its mechanical energy ($250\text{ J}$) is less than the required energy at D ($343\text{ J}$).
